## Exponential dispersion models

We say that a distribution belongs to the *exponential dispersion model* family if the distribution's probability function can be written in the form

$$f(y; \theta, \phi) = a(y, \phi) \exp \left\lbrace \frac{y \theta - \kappa(\theta)}{\phi} \right\rbrace$$

where $\theta$ is called the *canonical parameter*, $\kappa(\theta)$ is the *cumulant function*, $\phi > 0$ is the *dispersion parameter*, and $a(y, \phi)$ is a function -- which does not depend on $\theta$ -- that ensures $f(y; \theta, \phi)$ integrates or sums to 1.

## Normal distribution

The $N(\mu, \sigma^2)$ distribution has pdf

$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi \sigma^2}} \exp\left\lbrace-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}(y - \mu)^2 \right\rbrace$$

Show that the $N(\mu, \sigma^2)$ distribution belongs to the EDM family.
